about:
Industrial Semiconductor, Inc. was founded in 1991 by Fred Marquardt in Granville, Illinois. Marquardt’s career began in a radio and TV repair shop before he joined the United States Air Force, where he worked on vacuum tube and solid-state electronics. He later became part of the SCR development team at National Electronics, contributing to manufacturing innovations and serving on the JEDEC Industry Standards Committee. The business incorporated in 2004, and in 2015 ownership transferred to Steven Malavolti, a 20-year U.S. Navy veteran and former chief petty officer, who had joined the company in 2007 and became general manager in 2010.

The company operates as a mainline stocking distributor of high-power semiconductors, including SCRs, diodes, bridge modules, thyristor modules, diode modules, and GTOs from manufacturers such as Dynex, Times Electric, RIRI Power Electronics, GE, Westinghouse, Infineon, Powerex, Mitsubishi, Westcode, and IXYS. In addition to distribution, Industrial Semiconductor provides heatsink extrusion and assembles air-cooled thyristor, diode-heatsink, and SCR-heatsink assemblies. The Granville facility maintains an extensive inventory with same-day shipping and no minimum order requirement.

Customers span the power electronics, automotive racing, and renewable energy sectors. Early projects included solid-state timing systems for SCCA and NASCAR racing, as well as portable timing for Ford Motor Company’s road racing team. More recently, the company serves the wind turbine energy market and broader industrial power applications, working directly with engineers and OEMs who require technical problem-solving rather than transactional sales.

Industrial Semiconductor distinguishes itself by avoiding e-commerce automation in favor of direct voice and email contact, staffing technical problem solvers who know the product line. The company sells only new, factory-tested components to original OEM specifications, aiming to build a long-term team that can meet evolving power industry needs.

about:
Innovative Circuits Arizona (ICA) operates from Gilbert, Arizona, providing electronics contract manufacturing and CNC machining services. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

ICA runs a 3,000-square-foot surface-mount technology (SMT) area with controlled temperature, humidity, and ESD compliance, alongside through-hole assembly capabilities. Its CNC machining cell includes 3-, 4-, and 5-axis machines for metals, plastics, and specialty materials. The shop supports prototype through low- to medium-volume production, and offers in-house inventory management via a Juki ISM Fortress humidity-regulated tower, materials procurement, and a full test suite: in-circuit testing, functional testing, environmental stress screening, automated optical and X-ray inspection.

The company serves aerospace, medical, automotive, industrial, and telecommunications sectors, including automotive electronics and medical device customers. Its quality system is certified to AS9100 and ISO 9001, with adherence to IPC standards, though CNC machining and design fall outside the certified scope.

ICA emphasizes nimble, adaptable production to meet shrinking product lifecycles, combining rapid prototyping, real-time quality data loops, and scalable manufacturing to reduce time-to-market for clients in highly regulated industries.

name: Integra Life Sciences
old_description: Restoring Lives Through Everyday Impact: The Power of Small Actions
about:
Integra LifeSciences was founded in 1989 and is headquartered in Mansfield, Massachusetts. The company operates a manufacturing facility in Le Locle, Switzerland, where it produces valves for hydrocephalus management.

The company develops and manufactures medical devices across neurosurgery, wound reconstruction, soft tissue repair, surgical instrumentation, and ear, nose, and throat (ENT) solutions. Its product portfolio includes dural access and repair systems, cerebral spinal fluid management devices, regenerative technologies for complex wounds and burns, nerve and tendon repair products, and the CUSA® ultrasonic surgical aspirator platform. Integra also runs the BioSkills Lab, a hands-on training environment for healthcare professionals.

Integra serves surgeons, hospitals, and healthcare systems worldwide, with a focus on neurosurgery, plastic and reconstructive surgery, wound care, and ENT specialties. Clinical examples include the AERA® pediatric registry for ear tube procedures and the treatment of severe burn patients such as Tyler Schultz, who underwent more than 100 surgeries using Integra's regenerative technologies.

The company positions its manufacturing operations as purpose-driven, emphasizing evidence-based regenerative technologies and long-standing innovation such as the 20-year history of CUSA® technology. Its stated mission centers on restoring lives through everyday impact, combining global leadership in neurosurgery with immersive surgical education.

about:
Integrated Technology Solutions, LLC, doing business as ITS Hawaii, was founded in 2016 in Waipahu on the island of Oahu. The company operates as a licensed electronics system contractor (license CT-36449) serving the entire state of Hawaii, including Oahu, Maui, Kauai, the Big Island, Lanai, and Molokai.

ITS Hawaii specializes in low-voltage design, installation, and configuration for commercial and residential projects. Its service portfolio spans structured cabling, wireless access point deployment, IT rack build-outs, audio-video systems, home and business automation, digital signage, security camera and surveillance systems, point-to-point antennas, satellite dish and DIRECTV installation, and video conferencing infrastructure. As a Crestron authorized dealer, the firm integrates Crestron control and automation platforms into its projects. The company describes itself as a full-service digital signage and low-voltage contractor providing end-to-end technology network solutions.

The contractor serves a range of verticals including medical facilities, government and military installations, educational lecture halls, corporate boardrooms, and high-end residential properties. Customers include businesses requiring structured cabling and network upgrades, homeowners seeking automation and theater systems, and organizations needing security surveillance or digital signage deployments. A review from a home theater and automation company notes ITS Hawaii provides fiber optic terminations and networking support on a subcontract basis.

The company's stated mission is to improve clients' low-voltage infrastructure through new designs, craftsmanship, quality products, and customer service. Its differentiation rests on statewide reach, Crestron partnership, and a focus on tailored end-to-end solutions rather than product sales alone.

name: Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions (IMS)
old_description: With a focus on producing quality parts since 2005, we are well-equipped to meet the unique demands of each sector we serve.
about:
Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions (IMS) was founded in 2005 in Londonderry, New Hampshire. The company was purpose-built to address a service gap for high-quality, rapid prototype and small-lot printed circuit board assembly. The founders, whose names are not publicly disclosed, recognized the struggles businesses faced in receiving responsive customer service for prototype and low-volume PCBA needs. In December 2024, IMS was acquired by Perimeter Solutions (NYSE: PRM), which aims to broaden its portfolio and add a new business model for acquiring and supporting OEM legacy product lines.

IMS provides full life-cycle electronics assembly services, including rapid prototype assembly, high-mix flexible manufacturing, design-for-manufacturing (DFM) analysis, end-of-life support, box build, short-notice production, and build-to-order manufacturing. The New England facility houses multiple SMT pick-and-place lines (Mycronic MY300, M100, MY9E), three Heller 1808 MkIII reflow ovens, solder paste inspection and deposition equipment (Mycronic Primo 3D SPI, MY600, MY500, SpeedPrint SP710, MPM Accuflex), X-ray and AOI inspection (UniComp AX8200, Mirtec MV6 Omni), rework stations (VJ Electronics Summit), selective soldering (Nordson Novo 103, Ace 102, Hollis TDL wave), and aqueous cleaning systems. The company emphasizes quick turnaround, stating it can start production the day an order is received and ship assemblies within hours. No specific headcount or facility square footage is disclosed.

IMS serves aerospace and defense, medical and instrumentation, communications, consumer electronics/IoT, automotive, and industrial sectors. Customer testimonials cite an automotive technology company, a consumer robotics company, and an IoT solutions provider. The company supports OEMs needing rapid prototyping, low-volume production, and end-of-life product sustainment.

IMS was started to fill a market gap for responsive, high-quality prototype and low-volume PCBA services. The company differentiates itself through a culture of responsiveness, on-time delivery, and a direct order fulfillment model that helps customers grow. Its acquisition by Perimeter Solutions adds a model for acquiring and licensing OEM legacy product lines to sustain them through their remaining lifecycle.

about:
Inter-Coastal Electronics (ICE) operates from Mesa, Arizona, and serves as the current Tactical Engagement Simulation System (TESS) Program of Record holder for U.S. Army aviation. The company provides embedded training solutions built on three decades of experience in live, virtual, and constructive training environments.

ICE designs, develops, manufactures, tests, delivers, and supports live training systems that increase warfighter effectiveness and survivability. Its product portfolio includes TESS production kits with ground support equipment, the TOW-ITAS Laser Integrated Field Training System (LIFTS), the Training ASE Stimulation Suite (TASS), and the Army TADSS Maintenance Program (ATMP). The company handles engineering, production planning, depot repair, supply chain management, and systems integration for ruggedized electronics and embedded systems.

ICE supports U.S. Army aviation platforms at Combat Training Centers including the National Training Center (NTC), Joint Readiness Training Center (JRTC), and Joint Multinational Readiness Center (JMRC). International customers include the Netherlands, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, Qatar, and Morocco, with programs covering AH-64E Apache, UH-60M Black Hawk, CH-47F Chinook, and TOW missile systems.

The company emphasizes a low-risk, cost-effective approach that provides immediate interoperability with existing Army ranges and a Modular Open Systems Architecture (MOSA) to reduce lifecycle costs. Leadership includes veterans with extensive Army aviation and acquisition experience, guiding a strategy focused on readiness, proficiency, and affordability.

about:
Intercoastal Electronics EMS operates from Rockledge, Florida, as a full-service electronics contract manufacturer. The company focuses on complex printed circuit board assemblies that combine surface-mount, through-hole, fine-pitch, and specialty component technologies.

Its manufacturing services span prototype through low-to-mid-volume production, including SMT and through-hole PCB assembly, complex mixed-technology builds, system-level box build, inspection, conformal coating, and rework/repair. The firm also provides engineering support and component reconditioning, positioning itself as a partner for high-mix, flexible-volume programs.

The customer base comprises OEMs, engineering teams, and product developers seeking reliable, repeatable electronic assembly for commercial non-regulated products. Intercoastal emphasizes supply-chain continuity and overflow manufacturing, offering transparent quoting and production planning without hidden costs.

The company highlights its IPC-certified assembly and inspection processes as a quality differentiator, along with a disciplined approach that bridges prototype and production phases. Flexible capacity and expertise in challenging thermal and mechanical constraints are cited as reasons customers partner with Intercoastal.
